title: Checked programme proof scopes
scope: All 51 lessons and 36 mathematical prerequisite readings are self-checked, with 924 exact proof scopes. Four preserved source components have separate provenance and terms checks and links to complete programme proofs.

proof_nodes.complete_proof_locator: First two proof paragraphs, ending with the complex integral inequality.
proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: Arbitrary measure spaces; nonnegative increasing measurable functions, almost-everywhere convergence, and finite absolutely integrable complex functions.
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: Null sets have zero simple integral. Compare a simple minorant with c times that minorant on increasing comparison sets and use set continuity; let c increase to one and take the supremum, including infinite values. MCT gives nonnegative additivity and summable interchange. Positive/negative parts define real integration; real/imaginary parts give complex linearity. For z=integral u, multiplication by conjugate(z)/abs(z) if z is nonzero (one otherwise) proves the integral inequality by field algebra and modulus.

proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: Apply MCT to infima of tails; compare their integrals to the corresponding infima. Apply Fatou to 2g minus the absolute difference, whose pointwise limit is 2g outside the null exceptional set. Finite integral of g permits subtraction and proves norm convergence and convergence of integrals.

proof_nodes.complete_proof_locator: Essential-bound paragraph, algebraic p=2 paragraph and the full lemma proof specialized to these exponents.

Normalization gives Cauchy-Schwarz and then Minkowski; p=1/infinity are pointwise. A summable Cauchy subsequence has an Lp majorant by MCT and a pointwise scalar limit; its tails converge in norm. Infinity uses uniform convergence off one null set. Truncation to finite-measure level sets plus finite scalar grids and DCT proves density. Scalar integration gives inner-product axioms. The general real-exponent calculus step is expressly outside this node, with the full theorem preserved.

For finite measures, equality sets form a lambda-system because totals agree and are finite.

proof_nodes.complete_proof_locator: Entire proof including the tower comparison and the union of all towers.
proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: Every nonempty partially ordered set in which every chain has an upper bound.
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: Under no maximal element, choice selects an outside upper bound for each chain. Two towers are initial-segment comparable: the first divergence has the same predecessors and the same selected next point. The union of all towers is well ordered (choose one tower containing any given member to find the least element of a nonempty subset) and every tower is an initial segment. Adjoining its selected upper bound produces another tower and the contradiction. Only sets and choice are invoked.

proof_nodes.complete_proof_locator: Both paragraphs from the one-dimensional real functional through the final complex separation conclusion.
proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: Every real or complex normed space, including nonseparable and incomplete spaces; bounded functionals separate distinct vectors.
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: For the real one-dimensional extension, every lower candidate is at most every upper candidate by the triangle inequality. Candidate zero bounds both finite endpoints, so real completeness supplies the extension value. Positive and negative scalar cases prove the norm bound. Union of a chain of compatible extensions is a valid extension; the proved Zorn lemma gives maximal full domain. In the complex case f(x)-i f(ix) is complex linear and the explicit conjugate phase proves the bound; its real value at the chosen nonzero vector is positive.

proof_nodes.complete_proof_locator: #coordinate-linear-algebra, all four paragraphs before #coordinate-differential-rules
proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: Finite real coordinate norms/matrices, orthonormalization, determinant and inverse/elementary-matrix identities, including dimension zero.
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: Quadratic minimization proves Cauchy-Schwarz, then triangle and equivalent finite norms. Coordinate completeness, row bounds and submultiplicativity are explicit. Permutation expansion proves alternating determinant uniqueness, products, transpose and adjugate. Zero-kernel elimination is proved by induction, including the smaller-block kernel test and elementary factors. Gram-Schmidt and orthonormal extension give the positive Gram determinant. The zero-dimensional convention is retained.

proof_nodes.complete_proof_locator: All paragraphs before #continuous-primitives.
proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: Compact finite-dimensional sets, their continuous normed-space images and scalar extrema, uniform continuity, distance properties and the scalar mean-value theorem.
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: Reuse the nested-box compactness proof. Closed subsets are compact by adding the complement to covers; images by pullback of covers. Increasing bounded-value covers prove boundedness; nested closed near-supremum sets have a common point by finite-subcover contradiction, proving extrema. Finite ball covers prove compact sets closed. Triangle and infimum prove distance is Lipschitz; exterior openness and compact minima give positive separation. A finite smaller-ball cover proves uniform continuity. Interior extrema have zero derivative by the opposite one-sided signs; subtract the chord to prove the mean-value theorem.

proof_nodes.complete_proof_locator: The direct continuous real scalar proof through the sentence about the scalar application, before Fix t0 in J.

Additivity and the integral bound give the average-error estimate tending to zero by continuity, for either sign of h. Therefore the primitive derivative equals the integrand. Applied to u-prime, the mean-value theorem makes u minus its primitive constant. Real/imaginary or finitely many coordinate components give the stated versions. This direct scalar proof does not use vector integration, dual separation or a.e. differentiation.

proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: Normalize by the invertible derivative and take a closed r-ball with derivative error at most one half. CI1 proves injectivity and the inverse Lipschitz bound. The minimum for target norm below r/4 is interior because its boundary value exceeds its value at zero; the directional derivative equation and invertible transpose force a root. Compact extrema are an explicit earlier dependency. The separate contraction construction proves existence for every target below r/2, including completeness, convergence and uniqueness, preserving the larger former radius. The two-sided geometric matrix inverse and bound2 are retained as an alternative. The inverse Lipschitz bound converts the original differentiability remainder to o(k), then the matrix inverse identity gives C1. Local openness and global injective gluing are proved; triangular energy coordinates give CI3 with either derivative sign.

proof_nodes.complete_proof_locator: #coordinate-integration, entire Section3, CI4-CI5
proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: Every C1 diffeomorphism between open Euclidean subsets, with every nonnegative completed-measurable integrand and every absolutely integrable complex integrand.
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: Linear scaling is reduced to permutations, scalings and shears using the proved elimination and product measure. Cube coverings prove local Lipschitz null preservation in both directions, extended over countably many rational cubes. A closed small cube is trapped between outer and inner cubes after affine normalization. The inner inclusion follows from compactness, local openness and a proved clopen interval argument; the constructive contraction alternative is also retained. The exact (1 plus or minus 2epsilon)^n estimates are uniform on compact neighborhoods. Continuous tests follow from disjoint cube interiors and null image faces with uniform-error sums. Increasing compactly supported distance cutoffs prove equality on open sets; relatively compact exhaustion and the earlier finite pi-lambda theorem extend to all Borel sets, then null preservation to completions and simple approximation to nonnegative and absolutely integrable complex functions. Empty support and full Euclidean domains are explicitly covered.

proof_nodes.complete_proof_locator: #elementary-limits, entire section including EF1
proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: Scalar geometric and polynomial-geometric limits, absolute series products, intermediate values and continuity of monotone inverses on intervals.
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: Archimedean property follows by the supremum contradiction. Binomial lower bounds give geometric decay, and successive ratios bound polynomial factors by a larger geometric ratio. Finite geometric sums and completeness prove summability. Bisection proves intermediate values; neighboring image values prove inverse continuity. The explicit two-tail estimate controls all finite sums outside a square, hence diagonal and rectangular products have the same limit.

proof_nodes.complete_proof_locator: #scalar-exponential, entire section EF2-EF5
proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: Complex exponential on the entire plane, all derivatives and addition law; real positivity, monotonicity and bijection onto positive reals.
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: Factorial ratios prove uniform absolute convergence on every disk, also after polynomial factors in the index. The exact difference-of-powers factorization controls the derivative remainder by a convergent n-squared majorant. Diagonal multiplication and the finite binomial identity prove addition and nonvanishing. Conjugation proves real values, the half-argument square proves positivity, and the derivative proves strict increase. The series lower bound and reciprocal identity prove the endpoint limits; intermediate values give the range.

proof_nodes.complete_proof_locator: #logarithm-and-real-powers, entire section EF6-EF9
proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: Real logarithm on all positive reals; arbitrary real powers, their derivatives and positive-exponent extension to zero; all conjugate exponents in Young inequality; exponential decay against any real nonnegative power.
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: Continuous inverse difference quotients prove log derivative 1/x. Addition and injectivity give the logarithm law. The definition exp(a log x) gives all power identities and derivatives. Endpoint limits give continuity at zero and the needed right derivative. The derivative sign on either side of b^(1/(p-1)) proves the global minimum and Young inequality, including zero arguments. One positive term of the exponential series bounds y^M exp(-y) using an integer N>M.

proof_nodes.complete_proof_locator: #trigonometry-and-period, entire section EF10-EF12
proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: Real sine/cosine and their addition/derivative identities; complete unit-circle parametrization; exact period and the entire complex exponential kernel.
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: Conjugate exponential formulas give real functions, derivatives, parity, addition and the circle identity. If cosine has no positive zero, increasing positive sine forces cosine negative by its integral formula. Infimum and continuity give the first zero c. Strict monotonicity covers the first quadrant exactly once; quarter rotations cover the full circle with only shared endpoints. Integer reduction proves the exact period 4c=2pi. The modulus exp(real z) identifies the entire complex kernel. The unit speed checks circumference normalization.

proof_nodes.complete_proof_locator: #arctangent-and-poisson-kernel, entire section EF13-EF15
proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: Real arctangent on the whole line, its derivative and pi/4 value, total Cauchy-kernel mass pi, and the Poisson approximate identity for bounded measurable functions continuous at the evaluation point.
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: The quotient sine/cosine on the first two neighboring quadrants is strictly increasing with infinite endpoint limits. Its inverse derivative is 1/(1+x^2). Reflection about the quarter angle gives arctan(1)=pi/4. FTC and endpoint limits give total integral pi, and monotone convergence identifies the Lebesgue integral. Comparison with t^-2 gives the explicit tail. Linear scaling proves Poisson mass one; splitting near and far proves the stated approximation for bounded measurable inputs.

proof_nodes.complete_proof_locator: #smooth-flat-cutoffs, entire section EF16-EF18
proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: Smooth flat functions on the real line and compact bumps, plateau cutoffs and normalized mollifiers in every positive finite Euclidean dimension.
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: Induction expresses right derivatives as finitely many inverse powers times exp(-1/t). The exponential decay estimate controls each expression and its difference quotient, proving all derivatives at zero vanish. Positivity of the displayed denominator proves smooth plateau functions. Polynomial composition gives the ball bump. Compact boundedness and a positive lower bound on a small cube prove a finite positive integral. Length/product scaling normalizes dilations. Real-power smoothness justifies the square-root normalization of finite sums.

proof_nodes.complete_proof_locator: #complete-function-spaces, entire function-space lemma and proof

The elementary power bound first ensures a sum is in Lp; Holder against the (p-1)st power proves the triangle inequality. A summable-difference subsequence and monotone convergence produce the limit and tail norm estimates on any measure space. The essential-supremum proof removes only countably many measurable null sets. Truncations have finite measure support and dominated convergence; finite grid approximations give density. The already checked endpoint/L2 reasoning is preserved and uses no general-exponent circular input.

proof_nodes.complete_proof_locator: #strong-measurability, entire Section 1, (1)-(2) and (VI1)
proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: Real or complex Banach spaces, without separability of the ambient space; completed Euclidean measurable domains. Smooth finite-vector density on open time intervals and completeness of L1(B).
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: Countably many approximant values have a separable closed linear span (finite rational real/complex combinations form a countable dense set). Measurable distances and nearest among the first N dense values, including zero, give a finite-valued measurable approximation with error at most the norm of f. This proves closure under almost-everywhere limits and bounded maps. Scalar dominated convergence gives L1 convergence and the nonzero-cell estimate gives finite measure. Finite interval approximation, interior truncation and the explicitly proved step cutoff give smooth finite-vector density with compact support in the time interval. A summable subsequence of a Cauchy sequence converges pointwise by Banach completeness and in L1 by the summed scalar norm tails.

proof_nodes.complete_proof_locator: #bochner-integral, entire Section 2, (3)-(6) and improper integrals

Completion extends the integral by the L1 difference estimate; the summable-subsequence argument supplies strong measurability of its L1 limits. Tail differences form a Cauchy family, so completeness gives improper integrals with the scalar norm tail bound.

Explicit compact exhaustion and monotone convergence give the open-set bound. Continuous scalar L1 density bounds the exceptional outer measure by 4 times the approximation error divided by epsilon; a countable epsilon union is null. Compact truncation gives the local theorem. Apply it simultaneously to countably many distances in the essential separable range; retain the factor 2, then use density. One-sided averages are bounded by twice the symmetric averages.
